audits.standard: College of American Pathologists guidelines for FFP transfusion
audits.setting: Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi; tertiary trauma centre
audits.other_findings: Orthopaedics accounted for 12.6% of FFP use; neurosurgery had the highest appropriate use (50.5%).

audits.title: Improvement in intraoperative fresh frozen plasma transfusion practice--impact of medical audits and provider education.
audits.standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology FFP recommendations
audits.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi

audits.title: Clinical audit of the use of fresh-frozen plasma and platelets in a tertiary teaching hospital and the impact of a new transfusion request form.
audits.standard: NHMRC/ASBT Clinical Practice Guidelines for FFP and platelet transfusion
audits.setting: Tertiary teaching hospital, Royal Adelaide Hospital

cycle1.result: More than 72% of FFP and 88% of platelets prescribed appropriately (figures reported across the audit).

cycle2.result: Appropriate use further improved with the new request form, with satisfactory compliance (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Warfarin reversal was the main FFP indication (34%); room for improvement in haematology and cardiac bypass FFP use and surgical platelet use.
audits.citation: Hui CH, Williams I, Davis K. Clinical audit of the use of fresh-frozen plasma and platelets in a tertiary teaching hospital and the impact of a new transfusion request form. Intern Med J. 2005;35(5):283-288. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2005.00803.x. PMID: 15845110.

audits.title: Transfusion audit of fresh-frozen plasma in southern Taiwan.
audits.setting: Blood Bank, Kaohsiung Medical University Hospital
audits.intervention: Five education sessions on transfusion guidelines, then computerised transfusion guidelines with periodic audits by a consultant haematologist.

cycle2.result: Inappropriate requests fell to 30%; FFP transfusions fell by 74.6%. Education alone gave a 5.2% fall in inappropriate use and computerised guidelines a further 30%.

audits.other_findings: Education had a limited effect compared with computerised guidelines and periodic audit.
audits.citation: Yeh CJ, Wu CF, Hsu WT, Hsieh LL, Lin SF, Liu TC. Transfusion audit of fresh-frozen plasma in southern Taiwan. Vox Sang. 2006;91(3):270-274. doi:10.1111/j.1423-0410.2006.00819.x. PMID: 16958841.

audits.title: Population-based audit of fresh-frozen plasma transfusion practices.
audits.setting: Nine of 21 Finnish hospital districts (benchmarking project)

cycle1.result: Coagulation variables measured at any point in the episode in only 65.9% of FFP-transfused patients; FFP usually given in paired doses.

audits.other_findings: Surgery patients received FFP in 62.8% of transfusion hospital visits.

audits.standard: National Health and Medical Research Council and Australasian Society for Blood Transfusion guidelines for FFP use
audits.setting: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences, Karad

cycle1.result: Of 325 units, 197 (60.6%) in 67 patients were appropriate and 128 (39.4%) in 33 patients inappropriate.

audits.setting: Kecioren Training and Research Hospital emergency department, Ankara

audits.title: Plasma transfusion practices: A multicentre electronic audit.
audits.standard: Recommended indications and therapeutic dosing for plasma transfusion (electronic criteria)
audits.setting: Five academic hospital sites, multicentre electronic audit

cycle1.result: 77.7% of 6088 plasma transfusion events were outside indications or under-dosed; 34.8% of orders had no indication; 70.7% under-dosed.

audits.other_findings: Most transfusions in ICU or theatre; inter-hospital variability in testing and dosing.
audits.citation: Khandelwal A, Minuk L, Liu Y, Arnold DM, Heddle NM, Barty R, et al.. Plasma transfusion practices: A multicentre electronic audit. Vox Sang. 2022;117(10):1211-1219. doi:10.1111/vox.13355. PMID: 36102150.

audits.title: A retrospective audit to evaluate the appropriateness and rationalization of Fresh Frozen Plasma usage in a tertiary care hospital.
audits.standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology (2004, reviewed 2018) and College of American Pathologists (1994) FFP guidelines

cycle1.result: 51.8% of FFP transfusions inappropriate (3069 of 5922); 56.7% prophylactic.

cycle2.result: 22.3% reduction in the number of inappropriate transfusions (4858 FFP units).

audits.other_findings: INR under 1.5 times normal was the most common cause of inappropriate transfusion (15.08%).
audits.citation: Kumar S, Kushwaha N, Tomar A, Philip J, Biswas AK. A retrospective audit to evaluate the appropriateness and rationalization of Fresh Frozen Plasma usage in a tertiary care hospital. Med J Armed Forces India. 2022;78(Suppl 1):S226-S231. doi:10.1016/j.mjafi.2021.04.016. PMID: 36147414.

audits.title: A quality improvement initiative to reduce inappropriate plasma transfusions across community hospitals in the Niagara region.
audits.standard: Plasma appropriate when INR > 1.7 and dose 3-4 units in adults; aim to improve appropriateness by 25% over 12 months
audits.setting: Three community hospitals, Niagara Health, Ontario

cycle1.result: 42% of plasma transfusions in hospitalised adults were inappropriate.

audits.intervention: Awareness campaign, enhanced audit and feedback, technologist screening and an electronic transfusion order set in the EMR (PDSA cycles from July 2024).

cycle2.result: Median monthly appropriateness 90% (INR > 1.7), 89% (dose > 2 units) and 78% (both criteria).

audits.other_findings: Out-of-guideline requests screened by technologists fell by 15%; no significant change in plasma or red cell use.
audits.citation: Walter K, Ahmad I, Groeneveld T, Chander A, Refaei M. A quality improvement initiative to reduce inappropriate plasma transfusions across community hospitals in the Niagara region. Vox Sang. 2026;121(5):593-602. doi:10.1111/vox.70192. PMID: 41663313.

audits.standard: Appropriate indications for FFP transfusion in children
audits.setting: Tertiary paediatric hospital, Ankara City Hospital

cycle1.result: Appropriate FFP transfusion in 59% (587/987) of episodes; pre-transfusion coagulation tests in 674 (68%).
